Rashi on Eruvin 70b:10:1.hebrew: מבעוד יום - שעדיין לא קנה עירובו של ראשון, הרי זה מן השוק אוסר. ואע"פ שאינו דר כאן — כדתניא לקמן בהאי פירקא: מי שיש לו בית התבן ובית הבקר בחצר חבירו אוסר עליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:10:1.english: While it was still day - Since the first [resident's] eiruv had not yet acquired [the domain], this [person] from the marketplace renders [carrying] prohibited. And even though he does not reside here, [he still prohibits,] as is taught later in this chapter: "One who has a straw shed or a cattle shed in his fellow's courtyard renders [carrying] prohibited for him."

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:10:2.english: [If he died] after nightfall, he does not render [it] forbidden to him - For it was permitted for part of Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:11:1.english: And one from the marketplace - Who had a residence in this courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:11:2.english: While it was still day, he does not render [carrying] prohibited - For this [heir] will make an eiruv with his neighbors.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:11:3.hebrew: משחשיכה - דאינו יכול לערב, אוסר. ואי יורש מבטל רשות, אמאי אוסר:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:11:3.english: After nightfall - Since he is unable to establish an eiruv, he renders [carrying] prohibited. And if an heir can renounce [his] domain, why does he render [carrying] prohibited?

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:13:1.hebrew: ישראל וגר גרסינן - גר שמת ואין לו יורשין, המחזיק בנכסיו זכה בהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:13:1.english: We read: "An Israelite and a convert" - [In the case of] a convert who dies and has no heirs, whoever takes possession of his property acquires it.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:13:2.hebrew: מגורה - גורן הוא, וחלוק בחדרים, והיה לכל אחד פתחו בחצר, ואוסרין זה על זה:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:13:2.english: A storehouse - It is a granary, and partitioned into rooms, and each one had his doorway into the courtyard, and they restrict each other.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:1:1.hebrew: היכא דאי בעי לעירובי כו' - כלומר, אביו, שהיה אתמול ראוי לערב, היה יכול לבטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:1:1.english: Where, if he wanted to establish an eiruv, etc. - That is to say, his father, who was fit to establish an eiruv yesterday, could have renounced [his rights].

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:1:2.hebrew: אבל האי דלא מצי לערובי אתמול - דלא היה לו חלק בה — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:1:2.english: But this [heir], who could not establish an eiruv yesterday - For he had no share in it — [he can]not [renounce].

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:3:1.english: Anything that was permitted for part of Shabbat, etc. - [The Gemara] goes on to explain it.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג - כגון עירב דרך הפתח כו', זה הכלל לאתויי מבוי שניטלה קורתו או לחייו:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:4:1.english: This is the correct reading - “For example, [if] one established an eiruv via the opening, etc., this is the general rule: to include an alleyway whose crossbeam or side post was removed.”

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:4:2.hebrew: עירב דרך הפתח - שתי חצירות ופתח אחד ביניהם, ועירבו ע"י אותו פתח, ובשבת נפלה כנגדו מפולת ונסתם — מותרים להשתמש מזו לזו ע"י זריקה ודרך חורין קטנים. דאע"ג דאין עירוב בין ב' חצירות בלא פתח, כדתנן (לקמן עו א) בחלון שבין ב' חצירות — הכא, שבת — הואיל והותרה, הותרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:4:2.english: [If] one established an eiruv via the opening - [In a case of] two courtyards with a single opening between them, and they established an eiruv by means of that opening, and on Shabbat rubble fell in front of it and it was blocked — they are permitted to use [items] from this one to that one by means of throwing and through small holes. For even though there is no eiruv between two courtyards without an opening, as we learned in the Mishnah (below 76a) regarding a window that is between two courtyards — here, [with respect to] Shabbat, since it was permitted [at its onset], it remains permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:5:1.hebrew: זה הכלל לאתויי מבוי שניטלה קורתו או לחייו - בשבת, אע"ג דאשתקול מחיצות דידיה — שרי, הואיל ואישתרי בין השמשות. ומרישא לא שמעינן לה, דהתם איתנהו למחיצות, אבל הכא — לא. והכי אמרינן לה בשילהי פירקא קמא (דף יז:):
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:5:1.english: “This is the principle,” to include an alleyway whose cross beam or its side posts were removed - [That is, they were removed] on Shabbat: Even though its partitions were removed, [carrying in it] is permitted, since it was permitted at twilight. And we could not have learned it from the first clause, for there the partitions are [still] intact, but here they are not. And so we said at the end of the first chapter (17b).

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:6:1.hebrew: והקיפום נכרים מחיצה - דאסורין לבטל זה לזה כדי שישתמש בה אחד מהן, דהואיל ואי הוו בעו ערובי מאתמול, לא מצו מערבי. אבל אי לא הוה התם אלא חד בית — שרי, דמחיצה הנעשית בשבת מחיצה היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:6:1.english: And gentiles enclosed them with a partition - That they are forbidden to renounce [their domain] to one another so that one of them may make use of it, since had they wanted to make an eiruv yesterday, they could not have made an eiruv. But if there were only one house there, it would be permitted, for a partition made on Shabbat is a [valid] partition.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:7:1.hebrew: זה הכלל - דרישא נמי קאי אסיפא, לאתויי מת נכרי בשבת. דכיון דאי בעו לערובי מאתמול לא מצו מערבי, השתא נמי לא מבטלי. ומרישא דסיפא לא שמעינן לה אי לא אתי' בזה הכלל, דהתם לא מצו לערובי מאתמול כלל, אבל הכא מצו לערובי ע"י שכירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:7:1.english: This is the principle - [The phrase "This is the principle"] of the first clause also applies to the latter clause, to include [the case of] a gentile who died on Shabbat. For since, if they had wanted to establish an eiruv yesterday, they could not have established an eiruv, now too they cannot renounce [their rights]. And from the opening [case] of the latter clause, we would not have learned it if it had not come [to be included] by [the phrase] "This is the principle"; for there, they could not have established an eiruv yesterday at all, but here, they could have established an eiruv by means of renting.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:8:1.hebrew: חוץ מן המבטל רשות - ששכח ולא עירב, אע"פ שנאסר למקצת שבת, יש לו תקנה בשבת. ומדלא קתני: "חוץ משביטל רשות ויורש", שמע מינה: יורש — לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:8:1.english: Apart from one who renounces rights - [One] who forgot and did not join in the eiruv, even though [the courtyard] was prohibited for part of Shabbat, has a remedy on Shabbat. And since it does not teach: “Apart from one who renounced rights and an heir,” learn from this [that] an heir [may] not.

Rashi on Eruvin 70b:9:1.hebrew: אימא חוץ מתורת ביטול רשות - ויורש בכלל, דכרעיה דאבוה הוא, ותורת ביטול נוהגת בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 70b:9:1.english: Say: Apart from the category of renunciation of rights - And an heir is included, for he is his father's leg [i.e., his legal extension], and the category of renunciation applies to him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:10:1.hebrew: אחד מבני חצר שמת והניח רשותו לא' מן השוק מבעוד יום אוסר כו' - הך ברייתא איירי בהכי: דבן חצר מערב עם חבריו, אבל בן השוק אין מערב עמהם, אפי' כשירש מבעוד יום. ולא משום שלא יוכל לערב עמהן לפי שאינו דר שם — דמסתמא לא גרע בהכי לענין עירוב וביטול רשות, כיון דאסר עלייהו, כדקתני "מבעוד יום אוסר" — אלא אורחא דמילתא היא: דבן חצר רגיל לערב עם חבריו, שהוא צריך להשתמש בחצר כיון שהוא דר שם; אבל אותו שבשוק אין יכול לערב, לפי שאינו רגיל להשתמש. וקסבר האי תנא כמ"ד לקמן בפירקין (עירובין דף עב:): בית התבן ובית הבקר, הרי זה אוסר עליו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:10:1.english: "A resident of a courtyard who died and left his domain to one from the marketplace, while it was still day, renders [carrying] prohibited, etc." - This baraita is dealing with this [scenario]: that a resident of the courtyard joins in an eiruv with his fellows, but a person from the marketplace does not join in an eiruv with them, even when he inherited while it was still day. And [this is] not because he would be unable to join in an eiruv with them because he does not dwell there — for presumably he is no worse in this regard concerning eiruv and renunciation of rights, since he restricts them, as [the baraita] teaches: "While it was still day, he renders [carrying] prohibited" — rather, it is the common way of things: that a resident of the courtyard is accustomed to join in an eiruv with his fellows, as he needs to use the courtyard since he lives there; but that [person] who is in the marketplace cannot join in an eiruv, because he is not accustomed to use [the courtyard]. And this tanna holds in accordance with the one who says later in our chapter (Eruvin 72b): "[With regard to] a straw storehouse and an ox barn, this renders [carrying] prohibited for him."

Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:13:1.hebrew: תא שמע ישראל וגר כו' - קסבר רבא: דמכח הגר חשיב כמו יורש, דהוי כרעיה דאבוה; דאי לאו הכי, לא קשה מידי לרב נחמן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:13:1.english: "Come and hear: A Jew and a convert, etc." - Rava maintains that [one who acquires] by virtue of the convert is considered like an heir, who is [an extension of] his father's leg; for were it not so, it would not pose any difficulty to Rav Naḥman.

Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:1:1.hebrew: אבל האי כיון דאי בעי לערובי מאתמול לא מצי לערב - אפילו למ"ד לעיל (עירובין דף סז.) מבטלין גבי מת נכרי בשבת, יכול להיות דאין מבטלין; כיון דהתם הוא דאותו רשות שהוא מבטל עכשיו היה לו כח לבטל מאתמול, אלא שלא היה מועיל מפני הנכרי דאוסר. אבל הכא, האי רשות דמבטל השתא אין לו כח לבטל מאתמול, אלא משעה שירש, והוי כב' בתים בשני צידי רה"ר דאין מבטלין, דלא היה בידו רשות זה מאתמול. ולמאן דאמר לעיל נמי אין מבטלין — יכול להיות דזה מבטל, כדאמר: "יורש כרעיה דאבוה הוא":
Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:1:1.english: "But this [heir], since, if he wanted to establish an eiruv yesterday, he could not have established an eiruv" - Even according to the one who said above (Eruvin 67a) that [the residents] may renounce [their rights] in the case where a gentile died on Shabbat, it could be that [here] they may not renounce [them]. For there, regarding that domain which he is now renouncing, he had the power to renounce [it] yesterday, except that it would not have been effective because of the gentile who prohibited [carrying]. But here, regarding this domain which he is renouncing now, he did not have the power to renounce [it] yesterday, but only from the moment he inherited [it]; and it is like [the case of] two houses on two sides of the public domain, where they may not renounce [rights], as this domain was not in his possession yesterday. And according to the one who said above as well that they may not renounce [rights], it could be that this [heir] may renounce [them], as [the Gemara] says: "An heir is [like] his father's foot."

Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:7:1.hebrew: לאתויי מת נכרי בשבת - פירש בקונטרס: כיון דאי בעו לערובי מאתמול לא מצו מערבי, השתא נמי לא מצו מבטלי. ומרישא סיפא לא שמעינן ליה אי לא אתי ב"זה הכלל", דהתם לא מצו מערבי מאתמול כלל, אבל הכא מצו מערבי ע"י שכירות. משמע מתוך פירושו דאיירי דאתא נכרי מערב שבת, ובעי למימר דאין מבטלין כשמת, וכ"ש דאם לא מת, דבעי תרתי: שכירות וביטול. ולא יתכן, לפי מה שפיר' לעיל דהתם כולי עלמא מודו דמבטלין גבי "מת נכרי בשבת מהו"; אלא בדאתא נכרי בשבת איירי הכא. ואי לאו "זה הכלל", הוי אמינא דהכא מבטל, כיון דהאי רשותא דקמבטל הוי בידו מאתמול, ולא דמי לב' בתים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:7:1.english: To include a gentile who died on Shabbat - Rashi explained: Since, if they had wanted to establish an eiruv yesterday they could not have established an eiruv, now too they cannot renounce [their rights]. And from the opening [case] of the latter clause [of the baraita], we would not have learned this if it had not been included by "this is the principle"; for there, they could not have established an eiruv yesterday at all, but here, they could have established an eiruv by means of renting [his domain]. It is implied from his explanation that [the baraita] deals with a case where the gentile arrived on the eve of Shabbat, and it intends to say that they may not renounce [their rights] when he dies, and all the more so if he did not die, where two [actions] are required: renting and renouncing. Yet this cannot be, according to what we explained above, for there everyone agrees that they may renounce, in [the sugya addressing the question]: "If a gentile died on Shabbat, what is [the ruling]?" Rather, it is where the gentile arrived on Shabbat that [the baraita] is dealing with here. And were it not for "this is the principle", I would have said that here he may renounce [his rights], since this domain that he is renouncing was in his possession yesterday, and it is not similar to [the case of] two houses.

Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:8:1.hebrew: וקתני חוץ ממבטל רשות - פי' בקונטרס: דפריך לר"נ, דאמר: דמבטלין, מדלא קתני "חוץ ממבטל רשות ויורש", שמע מינה יורש לא. ודבר תימה הוא: מה דיוק הוא זה?! ור"ח פירש: דפריך לשמואל, דאמר: "אין מבטלין". וזה לשונו: "זה הכלל: כל שנאסר למקצת שבת, כגון שני בתים בשני צידי רה"ר — חוץ ממבטל רשות, אע"פ שנאסר למקצת שבת, משעה שביטל רשותו הותרה שאר שבת; לא שנא הוא, ל"ש יורש. מדקתני 'חוץ מן המבטל רשות', דייקי מיניה: כל מי שיש לו רשות עכשיו יכול לבטל. ופריק לה לברייתא הכי: חוץ מתורת ביטול, דכי איתא לאוסר מעיקרא והשתא בטל רשות הותרה לשאר שבת; לאפוקי יורש, דלא הוי ליה רשות הכא בעידנא דקדש היום ולא הוי ליה לערובי, דלא איתמר תורת ביטול אלא היכא דליכא עירוב, ומאן דלא יכול לערובי לא יכול לבטל רשותו", עכ"ל. אע"פ שהקושיות אחרות לר"נ, אין לחוש אם זאת לשמואל. ורבינו חננאל בעצמו פירש דמותבינן לר"נ, משמע מתוך פירושו ד"חוץ ממבטל רשות" קאי אשני בתים משני צידי רשות הרבים והקיפום נכרים מחיצות בשבת, שמועיל שם ביטול; והיכא דלא ביטלו זה לזה, קאמר דנאסר לכל השבת כולה. וקשה: דאם כן, מאי "נאסר למקצת שבת" דקאמר? ונראה לומר לפירושו: דאיירי בעירבו, וכיון שלא חל העירוב בתחילת השבת תו לא חייל כשבאו אחרי כן והקיפום בשבת. וכן מת נכרי בשבת — איירי כשעירבו מערב שבת ובטל עירובן מפני הנכרי, דכשמת תו לא חייל; אבל ביטול מועיל בתרוייהו, כדקתני "חוץ ממבטל רשות". ומדמהני ביטול ב' בתים, אע"פ שלא היה לו כח לבטל רשות של חצר זה מאתמול, דרה"ר היה — כל שכן יורש, דיש לו כח לבטל! וקשה לדבי שמואל, דאמרי: "אין מבטלין". והוא הדין דהוה מצי למיפרך מהך ברייתא לרב חסדא ורב ששת, דאמרי לעיל "אין מבטלין" גבי ב' בתים. ונראה: דלמאי דמשני "אימא חוץ מתורת ביטול", לא קאי אב' בתים, אלא אבני חצר ששכח אחד מהן ולא עירב, שיכול לבטל רשות באמצע השבת. ומיהו, אם נאמר לפי המסקנא כן, גם לדברי המקשה לדחוק על חנם לומר דקאי אב' בתים?! דבלאו הכי יכול להקשות, כמו שפירש ר"ח, ד"חוץ ממבטל רשות" דמשמע: דכל מי שיש לו רשות עכשיו יכול לבטל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 70b:8:1.english: "And it teaches: Apart from one who renounces rights" - Rashi explained that [the Gemara] poses a difficulty to Rav Naḥman, who said that [an heir] may renounce [rights], [inferring:] from the fact that it does not teach: "apart from one who renounces rights and an heir," conclude from it that an heir [may] not. And this is astonishing: What kind of inference is this?! And Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained that [the Gemara] poses an objection to Shemuel, who said: "They may not renounce [rights on Shabbat]." And this is his phrasing: "'This is the general rule: Anything that was prohibited for part of Shabbat, such as two houses on two sides of the public domain' — apart from one who renounces rights; even though it was prohibited for part of Shabbat, from the time he renounced his rights the rest of Shabbat is permitted; [there is] no difference [whether it is] he, no difference an heir. Since it teaches: 'apart from one who renounces rights,' we infer from it: anyone who has rights [in the property] now is able to renounce. And [the Gemara] resolves the baraita in this manner: 'apart from the halakhic category of renunciation,' meaning that when the one who causes the prohibition was present at the outset and now renounced his rights, it is permitted for the rest of Shabbat; to exclude an heir, who did not have rights here at the time the day became sanctified and could not establish an eiruv, for the halakhic category of renunciation was stated only where there is no eiruv, and one who cannot establish an eiruv cannot renounce his rights," until here are his words. Even though the other objections [in the sugya] are against Rav Naḥman, there is no concern if this [particular objection] is against Shemuel. And [even if] Rabbeinu Ḥananel himself explained that we raise an objection against Rav Naḥman, it implies from within his explanation that "apart from one who renounces rights" refers to the two houses on two sides of the public domain where gentiles enclosed them with partitions on Shabbat, where renunciation is effective; and [in a case] where they did not renounce [rights] to one another, [the baraita] states that it is prohibited for all of Shabbat. And this is difficult: For if so, what is [the meaning of] "prohibited for part of Shabbat" that it states? And it appears [correct] to say according to his explanation: that it deals with [a case where] they established an eiruv, and since the eiruv did not take effect at the onset of Shabbat, it no longer takes effect when [gentiles] subsequently came and enclosed them on Shabbat. And similarly, [when] a gentile died on Shabbat — it deals with [a case where] they established an eiruv on Shabbat eve and their eiruv was suspended on account of the gentile, so that when he died it no longer takes effect; but renunciation is effective in both of them, as it teaches: "apart from one who renounces rights." And since renunciation is effective for the two houses, even though he had no power to renounce rights in this courtyard yesterday, as it was a public domain — all the more so an heir, who has the power to renounce! And [this presents] a difficulty for the school of Shemuel, who say: "They may not renounce." And the same applies that [the Gemara] could have posed an objection from this baraita to Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet, who said above: "They may not renounce" regarding two houses. And it appears: that according to that which [the Gemara] answers, "Say: Apart from the halakhic category of renunciation," it does not refer to the two houses, but rather to the residents of a courtyard where one of them forgot and did not establish an eiruv, who can renounce rights in the middle of Shabbat. However, if we say so according to the conclusion, [why] also according to the words of the challenger strain unnecessarily to say that it refers to the two houses?! For [even] without this he could object, as Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained, that "apart from one who renounces rights" implies that anyone who has rights [in the property] now is able to renounce.
